intro: **Quick answer:** Use a professional provider, such as a post office, professional photographer, camera store, some pharmacies or some chain stores. Ask for 2 dye-sublimation prints that meet the Australian Passport Office guidelines: 35-40 mm wide x 45-50 mm high, head 32-36 mm, on glossy paper of at least 200 gsm.

> **Important:** The Australian Passport Office recommends a professional passport photo provider and does not recommend online photo services or apps. Use our tool to check or prepare a photo, but always confirm it meets the official guidelines before you apply.
**[Check my photo with the Australian passport photo checker →](/australian-passport-photo-checker)**

sections.heading: Who can take your Australian passport photo?

subsections.heading: Providers named by the Passport Office
content: The Passport Office lists these types of providers:

- post offices
- professional photographers
- some large chain stores with printing facilities
- many camera stores
- some pharmacies
- other reputable businesses

subsections.heading: Why a professional provider is recommended
content: Passport photos need dye-sublimation prints on heavy glossy paper, which most people cannot make at home. Professional providers also have the right background and lighting.
The Passport Office does not recommend online photo services or apps.

subsections.heading: What the Passport Office does not endorse
content: The Passport Office does not endorse particular providers. A provider being on a list, or saying it is approved, is not a promise that your photo will be accepted.
You are responsible for checking that your photos meet the [Australian passport photo requirements](/guides/australian-passport-photo-requirements).

sections.heading: What should you ask the provider for?

subsections.heading: 2 identical prints at the Australian size
content: Ask for 2 identical colour prints, 35-40 mm wide x 45-50 mm high, with your head 32-36 mm from chin to crown.
Say clearly that they are for an Australian passport, because other countries use different head sizes.

subsections.heading: Dye-sublimation prints on glossy 200 gsm paper
content: Ask the provider to confirm that the photos are printed by dye sublimation, not inkjet, on glossy paper of at least 200 gsm.
If they are not sure, choose another provider.

subsections.heading: Photos taken within the last 6 months
content: Your photos must be less than 6 months old when you apply. Get them taken close to when you plan to lodge your application.
Ask the provider not to retouch the photo, because retouching is not allowed.

sections.heading: How do you check the photos before you apply?

subsections.heading: Check size, background and head position
content: Measure the print with a millimetre ruler: 35-40 mm wide, 45-50 mm high, and 32-36 mm from chin to crown.
Check that the background is plain white or light grey, with no shadows.

subsections.heading: Check against the official examples
content: Compare your photo with the unacceptable examples in the official guidelines. Look for smiling, glasses, a tilted head, hair over the eyes, streaks and ink marks.
Our [mistakes guide](/guides/australian-passport-photo-mistakes) lists all of them with fixes.

subsections.heading: Use our checker for a quick second opinion
content: Photograph the print clearly, or use the provider's digital copy, and upload it to our [Australian passport photo checker](/australian-passport-photo-checker).
It flags head height, background, lighting and glasses problems. It cannot test the print or paper, and a pass is not an approval.

subsections.heading: Check the Australian embassy page for your country
content: If you are applying from overseas, check the website of the Australian embassy, high commission or consulate for your country. It explains how to apply where you live.
The photo rules are the same Australian rules wherever you apply.

subsections.heading: Studios that know the rules
content: Some embassy pages list local photo studios that are familiar with the Australian rules. Embassies do not endorse these studios, so still check your photos yourself.
If you are in London or elsewhere in the UK, ask any studio whether it can meet the Australian size, head size and print rules.

subsections.heading: Why a UK or local passport photo may not meet Australian rules
content: A UK passport photo is 35 x 45 mm, but the UK head size is 29-34 mm, smaller than Australia's 32-36 mm. Other countries use different sizes again.
A provider that prints local passport photos may also not print by dye sublimation. Ask before you pay.

sections.heading: Can you use a photo from a booth?

subsections.heading: Booth photos and the print, size and 6-month rules
content: A booth photo must meet the same rules as any other photo: 2 dye-sublimation prints on glossy paper of at least 200 gsm, the Australian size and head size, and less than 6 months old.
Some booths are set up for other countries' sizes, so check before you use one.

subsections.heading: Questions to ask before you pay
content:
- Does it print at 35-40 mm wide x 45-50 mm high?
- Will my head be 32-36 mm from chin to crown?
- Does it print by dye sublimation on 200 gsm glossy paper?
- Is the background plain white or light grey?

subsections.heading: Keep the receipt and the prints safe
content: Keep your receipt in case you need a retake. Store the prints flat in an envelope, away from moisture.
Ink marks and damage can make a photo unacceptable, so do not write on the front or bend the prints.

subsections.heading: Australian Passport Office
content: - [Passport photo guidelines](https://www.passports.gov.au/PhotoGuidelines): provider advice, print and paper rules

subsections.heading: Overseas applicants
content: The website of the Australian embassy, high commission or consulate in your country explains how to apply from there.

subsections.heading: Last updated
content: Last updated: 21 November 2026. We checked these rules against the official pages on this date.
Rules and file limits change, so we review this page every 3 months. Always read the official page on the day you apply.

faq.question: Where can I get an Australian passport photo near me?
faq.answer: Look for a post office, professional photographer, camera store, pharmacy or large chain store with printing facilities. The Passport Office names these types of provider but does not endorse any particular business. Ask whether they print by dye sublimation on 200 gsm glossy paper before you book.

faq.question: Can a pharmacy take my Australian passport photo?
faq.answer: Some pharmacies can. The Passport Office lists some pharmacies among its types of provider. Ask whether they print Australian passport photos by dye sublimation on glossy paper of at least 200 gsm, and whether they know the 32-36 mm head size rule, before they take your photo.

faq.question: Can I get an Australian passport photo in the UK?
faq.answer: Yes, if the studio can meet the Australian rules. A standard UK passport photo has a smaller head size range than Australia allows, so ask for the Australian size and a 32-36 mm head. Also confirm dye-sublimation printing on 200 gsm glossy paper. Check the Australian High Commission website too.

faq.question: How many photos do I need for an Australian passport?
faq.answer: You need 2 photos. They should be identical colour prints from the same photo, made by dye sublimation on glossy paper of at least 200 gsm, and less than 6 months old. Keep both prints clean and flat until you lodge your application.

faq.question: How much does an Australian passport photo cost?
faq.answer: Prices vary between providers and locations, so we do not quote a figure. Ask the provider for the price before your photo is taken, and check whether it includes a retake if something is wrong. Compare a few local options if you can.

cta.title: Check the photos you get back
cta.text: Upload a clear copy of your photo to check head height, background, lighting and glasses. A pass is a guide, not an approval.
